The child updates the program’s financing history, immediate shortfall, and requested amounts. C25 has a weaker parallel emergency-relief appeal built around exhausted resources and an exact funding request, while C16 merely shares the generic form of an urgent appropriation request.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"This program of relief to Arab refugees displaced from Palestine was carried on during the fiscal year 1951 through contributions from participating countries, including a contribution from the United States of $25,450,000.","parent_excerpt":"The Congress appropriated $16 million for this purpose. Our contribution has been more than equalled by the contributions of 32 other countries.","explanation":"Both recount the same Palestine-refugee program through the history of U.S. and other participating-country contributions."},{"child_excerpt":"Available resources are now nearly exhausted.","parent_excerpt":"The fund thus raised has been stretched to its limits and is now exhausted.","explanation":"The child closely reuses C03’s concrete exhausted-funds predicate to justify renewed congressional financing."},{"child_excerpt":"One of the principal causes of tension in the Near East is the miserable state of the hundreds of thousands of Arab refugees from Palestine.","parent_excerpt":"The problems of Palestine and her neighbors are complicated by the continuing plight of over three-quarters of a million persons who left their homes during the conflict in Palestine, and are now refugees in the neighboring lands.","explanation":"Both frame the refugees’ condition as a regional political problem, not solely a humanitarian concern."},{"child_excerpt":"I therefore urgently request that the pending continuing resolution provide $2,000,000 for the month of August and $3,000,000 for the month of September.","parent_excerpt":"I, therefore, recommend that the Congress authorize and appropriate $27,450,000 for an eighteen month period.","explanation":"The operative request retains the same machinery—a presidential request that Congress appropriate a specified sum for a specified period—while adapting it to a temporary funding crisis."},{"child_excerpt":"Such a contribution is essential to prevent the starvation of many refugees and to avoid a deterioration in the present critical situation in the Near East.","parent_excerpt":"Not only is it consistent with the humanitarian spirit of the American people; it is also in our national interest to help maintain peaceful and stable conditions in the Near East.","explanation":"Both close the funding case by pairing humanitarian necessity with the preservation of stability in the Near East."}]}
